title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
statement: Swap every two adjacent nodes of the list, given as values, and return the new sequence. The values move with the nodes. Do not just swap the values in the algorithm: rewire next pointers.
hints: A dummy node points at the original head so the first swap is uniform.
Given prev, a, b, the rewiring is prev.next = b, a.next = b.next, b.next = a.
Then move prev to a, which is now the second node of the pair, and repeat while two nodes remain.

approaches.name: Swap values
approaches.explanation: Shorter and rejected when the interviewer wants pointer rewiring.

editorial: Build the nodes, then walk pairs from a dummy head. Each iteration rewires three pointers and advances by two nodes. A trailing single node is left in place because the loop requires two successors.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def swap_pairs(head: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    class Node:
        def __init__(self, value: int, nxt=None):
            self.value = value
            self.nxt = nxt

    dummy = Node(0)
    current = dummy
    for value in head:
        current.nxt = Node(value)
        current = current.nxt
    prev = dummy
    while prev.nxt and prev.nxt.nxt:
        first = prev.nxt
        second = first.nxt
        first.nxt = second.nxt
        second.nxt = first
        prev.nxt = second
        prev = first
    out = []
    node = dummy.nxt
    while node:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.nxt
    return out
